question: Will AfD win an absolute majority of seats in Sachsen-Anhalt?
thesis: Seat-arithmetic read, not news. An absolute seat majority under the Landtag's 5% threshold needs AfD's vote share divided by (1 - wasted share) to exceed 0.5. With AfD in the high-30s/40 range and the structurally wasted block (Gruene, FDP, micro-parties) around 10-12%, AfD lands ~44-46% of seats; a majority needs either a vote share of ~44%+ or BOTH SPD and BSW (each hovering near 5%) falling below the threshold so the wasted block exceeds ~20%. The double-threshold-failure path is real but conjunctive, and the 6-Sep-2026 date leaves little room for a late surge; the crowd's 25.5% prices that path at roughly twice what the conjunction warrants.

question: Will SPD win the most seats in the 2026 Mecklenburg-Vorpommern parliamentary elections?
thesis: Ladder-consistency leg of the frozen 2026-08-25 read: I froze AfD-most-seats at 0.85 (market .875). The residual mass belongs almost entirely to the incumbent SPD (Schwesig), since CDU/Linke are far from first place in MV; 0.12 for SPD plus ~0.03 for everything else closes my ladder. Small edge, logged mainly for calibration coherence across the event.

question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
thesis: Complement of the frozen 2026-08-23 read (GOP House at 0.17 vs market .12). Midterm-penalty base rates favour the out-party strongly, but a 4-seat margin flipping is not a 7-to-1 certainty ten weeks out: redistricting fights, incumbency retention and the 2022 precedent of a much smaller-than-expected wave keep the GOP hold tail fatter than the crowd's 11.5%. Logged for calibration coherence with the earlier leg.

question: Will Dan Sullivan win the Alaska Senate race in 2026?
thesis: Complement of the frozen 2026-08-25 read (Peltola at 0.50 vs market .61). Alaska is R+8 with a two-term incumbent senator; Peltola's 2022 special-election win came against a split Republican field under RCV and her 2024 House loss showed that advantage evaporating once the R side consolidated. The crowd's 61/39 for the challenger over-weights her personal brand relative to state partisanship in a race where the R vote is consolidated behind one incumbent.

question: Will Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins win the 2026 Alaska governor election?
thesis: Ladder-consistency leg of the frozen 2026-08-27 read (Wilson at 0.48 vs market .355). If P(Republican wins) is ~0.55-0.60 in an R+8 state with two Ds and two Rs in the RCV general, the Democratic mass splits between Kreiss-Tomkins and Begich; assigning K-T ~0.25 and Begich ~0.15 closes the ladder. The crowd's 31.5% for a Democrat with no statewide win history leans on Peltola-style optimism that the 2024 House result already contradicted.

question: Will Mark Sutcliffe win the 2026 Ottawa mayoral election?
thesis: Incumbency base-rate read on a thin market. Sitting Ottawa mayors seeking re-election have essentially always won (Watson three times, Chiarelli, O'Brien lost only after an ethics scandal), and the challenger field priced by the crowd is fragmented with the nearest name at ~17%. Absent a scandal I cannot see, a first-term incumbent against a fragmented field is nearer 75-80% than the crowd's 64.5%; confidence capped by the eight-month knowledge gap and low volume.

question: Will Olivia Chow win the 2026 Toronto mayoral election?
thesis: Same incumbency read as Ottawa: Toronto has not unseated a sitting mayor at the ballot box since amalgamation (Lastman, Miller, Ford-era Tory all held or retired), and the challenger mass here is a single councillor priced at 12.5% with no consolidated right-of-centre alternative. Edge barely clears the fee floor; logged as a calibration point, not a conviction bet.

question: Will Gavin Newsom announce a Presidential run before 2027?
thesis: Announcement-timing base rate, not a read on whether he runs. Serious major-party contenders overwhelmingly make the official 'I am running' announcement in the calendar year AFTER the midterm (2019, 2015, 2007 cycles); the only pre-midterm-year announcement by a front-runner in modern memory was Trump in Nov 2022 as an ex-president. Newsom is governor through early January 2027 and gains nothing from formalising before his term ends; exploratory noise, book tours and podcast hints do not meet this market's 'officially announces running' criterion. The 12.5% is a tail I would put nearer 5-8%.

question: Will Kamala Harris announce a Presidential run before 2027?
thesis: Same announcement-timing base rate as Newsom, with a weaker candidate rationale on top: Harris passed on the 2026 California governor race and has said she will decide on 2028 later; a losing nominee re-announcing before the midterm year has no modern precedent (Gore 2002 declined; Kerry 2006 declined; Clinton announced April 2015 for 2016). 9.5% over-weights headline chatter relative to the official-announcement criterion.

question: Ukraine election held by December 31, 2026?
thesis: Conditional-chain read using the crowd's own sibling prices. A national election requires martial law to be lifted, which requires a ceasefire, and Ukrainian law then needs roughly 60-90 days of organisation; so P(election held by 31 Dec) is bounded above by P(ceasefire by ~end-Oct) x P(martial law lifted promptly AND vote organised inside the remaining window). The crowd prices ceasefire-by-Oct-31 at ~8.5%; even a generous 30% conditional gives ~2.5%, and the market's own rule that an out-of-window scheduling resolves NO removes the 'announced but not held' upside. 5.5% is twice the chain's ceiling.

question: Will Russia test a nuclear weapon by December 31 2026?
thesis: Base-rate read on a hard criterion (actual chain-reaction detonation; subcritical experiments and delivery-system tests such as Burevestnik/Poseidon do not count). Russia has conducted zero explosive tests since 1990 and has repeatedly tied any resumption to a prior US test; the Trump-era 'resume testing' rhetoric has so far produced no US detonation and NNSA readiness is measured in months-to-years, so the conditional path (US tests first, Russia answers inside the same four months) is a product of two small probabilities. The wide 5.7/8.1 book and 6.9% mid reflect headline risk on missile tests that this criterion excludes.

question: Will Yulia Navalnaya win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2026?
thesis: Ladder leg consistent with the frozen Nobel tails (Trump .006, Zelenskyy .015, Pope Leo .01, UNRWA .015). Bookmaker/market favourites have a poor hit rate with the Norwegian committee, which since 2022 has alternated between institutional and grassroots laureates and gave the 2025 prize to Machado; a second consecutive prize to an exiled opposition figure against an authoritarian state is possible but is the kind of repeat the committee tends to avoid. 8.5% as the single most-likely named tail is defensible as a favourite, but the field ('other') carries most of the mass.
